questions.question: Which of the following do you NOT need to check before every ride?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Check the rims and spokes for bends, looseness, or damage. Check your tire condition and tread. Check all lights. You do not need to check the seat fabric.

questions.question: How can you increase your chances of being seen at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to draw attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at intersections to be more visible. Ride in a lane position where oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take quick action if needed.

questions.question: When downshifting, what should you do?

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Downshift one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch slowly between each downshift.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction for tires. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: What is usually found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars build up in the center of lanes. It is usually safe for a motorcycle to ride on this strip unless the road is wet.

questions.question: When braking, what should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time. Using both brakes together stops your motorcycle most effectively.

questions.question: Can proper clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Good clothing reduces crash injuries. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Choose sturdy material and make sure they fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing a lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position has several benefits. Most importantly, choose a position where other drivers can see you. Also make sure you have enough space around your motorcycle to react quickly if needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show traffic rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: To get the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: A horn on a motorcycle:

options.text: Should always be sounded when riding in fog.

questions.explanation: A street-legal motorcycle must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to look if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can assume drivers will see your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Keep enough distance between you and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: To give yourself time and space to spot and react to hazards.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keeping distance gives you space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of hazards on the road, like potholes.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it can be done before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden on a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have experience. Explain how to ride safely as a passenger.
Do not let them ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have experience. Explain how to ride safely as a passenger.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to know how to stay safe on a motorcycle. Never assume a passenger knows what to do. Always give clear instructions before each ride.

questions.question: Why is it better to ride in a small group?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders have to catch up to the group constantly.
It is hard to keep track of everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups have many advantages. Other vehicles can pass them more safely. They are less likely to be separated by traffic or traffic lights. Slower riders do not have to rush to catch up.

questions.question: What kind of helmet gives the best protection?

options.text: One that is old and broken in.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It must fit snugly around your whole head and have no cracks or damage.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be used on curves.
It should drive on the shoulder when turning.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or a motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves in a different way than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.
